subtopic: CUDA / Attention — naive scaled dot-product vs materialized attention matrix
learningObjective: Reason about the memory-traffic footprint of naive attention and identify the main bottleneck for long sequences.
stem: In a naive scaled-dot-product attention `O = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d)) V` implemented as three separate kernels (compute S = QK^T, materialize P = softmax(S), compute O = PV), Q/K/V/O are FP16 with shape `[B, H, S, D]`. Which statement about memory traffic on A100 is correct?

options.text: Because Q, K, V are FP16, all intermediate tensors including P and S are automatically kept in registers by the CUDA compiler; there is no HBM traffic for the S × S intermediates regardless of S.
The naive path is limited by the D×D dot product's compute cost, not memory; the S×S intermediate is only S*S/32 elements after warp-level reduction and never materialized in HBM.
Attention is compute-bound at all sequence lengths on A100 because FP16 matmul throughput is far higher than HBM bandwidth; the O(S^2) memory issue is a theoretical concern with no practical impact.

For each (batch, head), the naive path allocates and stores the `S × S` intermediate P (and S) in HBM: `2 * S^2 * sizeof(FP16)` bytes per (batch, head). For `S = 8192`, that is ~256 MB per (B,H) — the O(S^2) memory footprint is the dominant cost and grows quadratically with sequence length, making it infeasible for long sequences.

explanation: In naive three-kernel attention, the intermediate scores `S = QK^T` (shape [S, S] per head) and the softmax output `P = softmax(S)` (same shape) must be written to and read from HBM between kernels because register/SMEM is insufficient. The size is O(S^2 * sizeof) per (batch, head). For B=1, H=1, S=8192, FP16 that is 8192*8192*2 = ~128 MB for S plus another ~128 MB for P; with many batches/heads this dominates HBM traffic and quickly becomes infeasible. This is precisely the problem FlashAttention solves via tiled online-softmax computation that never materializes S/P.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: FP16 doesn't imply register residency of S×S intermediates.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: intermediates are per-thread partial values and cannot avoid being materialized in HBM without a tiled algorithm.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: at large S, HBM traffic for S×S dominates.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: naive attention has O(S^2) HBM footprint per (B,H).

assumptions: Three-kernel naive implementation without tiled online-softmax.
FP16 storage of Q/K/V/O and intermediates.
nonImplications: Does not imply naive attention is always slower than FlashAttention; for very small S it can be comparable.
Does not imply FP16 intermediates are numerically fine; some intermediates need FP32 for stability.

distractorRationales.A: Wrong claim about automatic register residency.

performanceClaim.scope: Naive attention HBM footprint at S=8192 FP16 on A100
